clue.text: Win over church member

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A congregation tries to recruit a fellow worshipper.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate them, winning them over by personal appeal.

clue.text: Managed to enter church with American writer

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, as a person enters a building

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ran a business means managed it

explanation.surface: Someone got into a church service accompanied by a famous American author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with American writer' reads as part of the story, but the writer alone is the definition and 'with' just joins it on.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Crane was the American novelist who wrote The Red Badge of Courage.

clue.text: Married, waving fan

indicators.note: something waving moves about, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly married couple wave to a fan in the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiast or devotee of someone, which is what an admirer is.

clue.text: A piece of cake for elderly guy after bread!

indicators.note: the words before 'after' are placed behind the word that follows it

parts.note: bread is slang for cash
taken as written
a plain synonym
a guy is a guy rope, steadying a tent

explanation.surface: An old man is handed a slice of cake after he has eaten some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Money for old rope is a British idiom for payment for very easy work; 'A piece of cake' also means something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for something achieved with no effort at all, the cake one generic and the rope one about easy earnings.

clue.text: Animals run away if beset by insects

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: ants are insects
to elope is to run away, usually to marry

explanation.surface: Wild beasts flee when plagued by swarming insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run away' is two words for one idea, the marriage sense of fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are a group of hoofed grazing animals, so they are an example of animals.

clue.text: A Chartered Accountant trained up in the scholarly world

parts.note: taken as written
CA is the abbreviation for chartered accountant

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: trained a gun on a target means aimed it

explanation.surface: A qualified accountant was educated in the world of the universities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' looks like it describes the accountant's education but means pointed, as with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities, scholarship and research.

clue.text: Soldier trapped in overturned vehicle — that's very sad

indicators.note: something trapped in a place is enclosed by it, so one word goes inside the other
an overturned thing is upside down, so in a down entry the word is read the other way

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier caught in a vehicle that has rolled over is a sad story.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something causing great sorrow, which is a heightened kind of sad.

clue.text: Mormons, say, translated it differently

indicators.note: doing something differently means arranging it in another way, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: Mormon scholars rendered a text in their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the 'for example' after 'Mormons', but its letters belong in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is the official name of the Mormon church, whose members are so called.

clue.text: US writer's heroine, Emily Dickinson perhaps

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, American writer of tales of horror
Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: The leading female character of an American writer might be the poet Emily Dickinson.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive in 'writer's' is just glue; Poe and Tess are joined side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson was an American poet, and poetess is the older word for a female poet, so she is an example.

clue.text: Deficit showing sharp drop

parts.note: a sharp, curt reply is a short one
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A budget gap is revealed by a steep decline in figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is an amount by which something falls short of what is needed, the same as a deficit.

clue.text: Song about soldiers in a republic

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
soldiers in the ranks are the men

explanation.surface: A song about troops, sung somewhere in a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins wordplay to definition; it does not signal an insertion here.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a former Soviet state in the Caucasus, now an independent republic.

clue.text: Traced awfully old design style

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone copied an old-fashioned decorative pattern very badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, so it is an example of a design style.

clue.text: What a golden handshake may bring in the near future? Seclusion

definitions.text: What a golden handshake may bring

parts.note: something happening early comes soon, ahead of time
retirement in the older sense of withdrawal from society

explanation.surface: An employee wonders whether a payoff will come soon and leave them in quiet isolation.
explanation.walkthrough: A golden handshake is a large payment to someone leaving a job, often to encourage them to go before they must.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous severance payment is often offered to persuade someone to stop working before the usual age.

clue.text: Mocking lecturer wearing traditional garment, cape

indicators.note: someone wearing a garment is inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: the sari is the traditional dress of Indian women
a don is a university lecturer
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A scornful academic dressed in traditional clothes with a cloak over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like another garment but is the geographical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic means grimly mocking or scornful, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Ferocious cur, he's a New Zealand dog

indicators.note: a ferocious creature is wild, so these letters are thrown into a wild new order

parts.note: taken as written
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand

explanation.surface: A vicious mongrel turns out to be a Kiwi hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The schnauzer is a German breed of wire-haired dog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Rum does it, and port

indicators.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange, so these letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Drinks talk: rum does the trick, and so does port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' and 'port' both look like drinks; one is an adjective meaning odd, the other a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is the major Black Sea port city of Ukraine.

clue.text: Mishandles a situation at college following mix-ups

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first piece named goes second

parts.note: a plain synonym
a student who is up is in residence at university

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles things at university after a series of muddles.
explanation.definitionFit: To mess something up is to spoil it through clumsy handling, the phrasal-verb equivalent of mishandling.

clue.text: Bully boy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to browbeat or intimidate
second meaning: a male first name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a noun phrase, a bullying lad, but 'Bully' is a verb and 'boy' a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to talk to someone in an intimidating way, and Hector is also a boy's name, from the Trojan hero.

clue.text: Whistle at referee's decision after bit of controversy

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word is used, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
an official's ruling in a game is a call

explanation.surface: Fans whistle at a disputed refereeing decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the selected letter before the rest; the referee's whistle in the surface is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a shrill whistle or jeer of disapproval, here as a noun.

clue.text: 'Exceedingly healthy', or just 'all right'?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally, in excellent health
second meaning: an expression of agreement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is in fine health or merely okay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means in great health, and is also a set phrase of assent, as in 'very well, I'll come'.

clue.text: Outshine famous racehorse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to surpass, throwing others into the shade
second meaning: the unbeaten 18th-century English champion

explanation.surface: A legendary horse beats all its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to overshadow by being better, and Eclipse was an undefeated racehorse whose name is still a famous stakes race.

clue.text: Turn down quantity of Chinese food

parts.note: to dim lights is to turn them down
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: A diner refuses a large portion of Chinese cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Cantonese dumplings and snacks, so they are an example of Chinese food.

clue.text: Book a room in Earl's Court that's vacant and in need of refurbishment

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something to be refurbished gets done over, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: a study is a room for reading and writing
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: a vacant word is emptied of its middle, leaving just its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Reserve an empty, run-down flat in Earl's Court, a district of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like the verb 'reserve' but is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1887 novel by Arthur Conan Doyle in which Sherlock Holmes first appears.

clue.text: Come to toddler with a touch of laryngitis

parts.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written

indicators.note: only a touch is used, the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor attends a little child with a slight sore throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to' suggests reviving, but here it means amount to.
explanation.definitionFit: To total is to add up to a figure, as a bill comes to fifty pounds.

clue.text: Devoted — many, but not quite all, in god's embrace

indicators.note: to be in someone's embrace is to be held inside their arms, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Zeus is the chief of the Greek gods

indicators.note: not quite all of the phrase is kept, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: A devout follower, among many but not all, held in a deity's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOT loses its last letter and the remainder goes inside ZEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealous means full of fervent enthusiasm for a cause, as a devoted follower is.

clue.text: Where children play could make one spit!

definitions.text: Where children play could make one spit!

parts.note: surface reading: a playground feature for small children
setter's reading: a mouthful of its grainy filling would make anyone spit it out

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plain; the joke is that the place is full of something children get in their mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit filled with sand is a standard play area for young children in parks and gardens.

clue.text: Helpful chart?

parts.note: surface reading: a useful diagram that gives assistance
setter's reading: 'help' here suggests the aid sense of a word that also means raised contours

explanation.walkthrough: Relief means help, but it also means the raised shaping of land; such a chart shows hills and valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing the height of the land, by shading or modelling, is named after relief in the sense of elevation.

clue.text: To rob reportedly requires nerve

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to rob is to take without permission

explanation.surface: Committing a robbery takes courage, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel, as in nerves of steel, means courage or resolve, a figurative sense of nerve.
